In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the propensity of the N-alkyl ester bond of the carbamic acid O-aralkyl ester to be cleaved in solution is a key factor for the inhibitory activity of this compound class.
the higher the propensity of the carbamic ester bond to be cleavage, the lower the inhibitory potency of the compound.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C(O)--N and C(O)--O bonds in the carbamic acid ester moiety are cleaved in a stepwise fashion.

FAAH-inhibiting carbamic acid O-(4-substituted-phenyl) esters are characterized by a low critical energy for the decomposition of their protonated molecules, which leads to the formation of the corresponding carbamic acid and the aryl cation, and this is related to their FAAH-inhibition activity.

the FAAH inhibitory activity of N-alkylcarbamic acid O-phenylethyl esters is correlated with their propensity to decompose by a process involving C(O)--O cleavage, and that such propensity is reflected in the energetics (i.e., the crossing point) of the [MH](+) --> [MH](+)(-CO) and [MH](+)-(CO)(-O) --> [MH](+) decomposition channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energetically more favourable the cleavage of the C(O)-O bond, the more active the compound as a FAAH inhibitor.
the mass spectrometric approach is a useful and reliable method to predict the FAAH-inhibiting activity of carbamic acid O-arly esters.
the C(O)--C bond cleavage is a key event in the decomposition of the protonated molecule and that the energy needed to break this bond is linearly related to the FAAH inhibitory activity.
